{"notes": "Visit 1 (left at 1:45). Plan: fish, Sofia's idea. Roles stated: Sofia = nose + top body line, Omar = bottom body line, Hana = top tail half, Jack = bottom tail half. I don't know who placed which dominoes, so these are claims plus what I saw in the picture.

Sofia: Proposed the fish and assigned roles clearly, including Hana's tail cue. Said at 1:30 the top line was almost at the tail. The picture backs this up: the top line is connected to the start and reaches about x=22.5 near the tail. Good so far on execution and leadership. Not yet judged on impact or collaboration beyond coordination.

Omar: Said at 1:30 the bottom line was 17 of 38 placed, about halfway. In the picture the bottom line is connected to the start but stops around x=17.5, with a gap of about 5 units still to reach the tail. His count matches what I saw. He plans to check the tail joint. He's the critical path now: the bottom line is the slowest part, and Jack's work is waiting on it. Watch his pace.

Hana: Said nothing in my visit. Her hands were at the end of the top line near the tail, so she may be starting her top tail half. Not yet verified. Need more evidence on her contribution.

Jack: Credited Sofia's idea and was clear about his role. He is waiting for the bottom line to reach the tail before laying his half, so he's idle for now. His hands were at the tail end. Ask next time whether he could help Omar or prep the tail.

Team: Everyone plans to check for gaps, which is good but redundant. The tail is still open at the bottom. Next visit: check whether the bottom line closes and whether the tail joins up cleanly."}
